Master.g1.label: Request submitted

intake.submission_channels.summary: A request may be delivered by hand, by first class mail to the RAO's business address, or by electronic mail to the posted address (regulations add facsimile if the custodian has fax access).

intake.oral_request_permitted.summary: Requests may be made orally in person to a records access officer or custodian; telephone requests may be accepted at the RAO's discretion.

intake.no_required_form.summary: A records access officer shall not require requesters to use a particular form, though optional forms may be made available.

Master.g1.city_config: Which channels the city actually operates (portal / form / paper / phone) — statute constrains, city chooses.

payment.nonpayment_consequence.summary: A records access officer shall not charge a fee for a public record unless the RAO responded to the requestor within 10 business days under subsection (b).
payment.nonpayment_consequence.clock_spec: terminal: fee right is forfeited if no § 10(b) response within 10 business-days

payment.nonpayment_consequence.summary: The RAO may deny public-records requests from a requester who has failed to compensate the entity for previously produced public records.
When denying for an unpaid balance, the RAO shall provide written notification detailing the reasons, including an itemized list of balances attributed to previously produced records.

Estimate-Fee.cnp.city_config: ⚠ nonpayment close window: statutory MO 90d · OR 60d · TX 60d · MI 45d (deposit); else city default (recommend 60d).

Denial.nreason.label: Select reason(s) from config library

denial.reasons_and_citation_required.summary: A denial/withholding must identify the records withheld and provide the specific reasons, including the specific statutory exemption(s) or common-law privilege and its applicability to each withheld portion.

Where a record is withheld on a claim of attorney-client privilege, the written denial must provide a detailed description of the record, including the names of the author and recipients and, in general terms, the subject matter of the withheld information.

Denial.nreason.city_config: The exemption/reason library itself is per-state config content (Phase-7 data load), keyed to statute cites.

Denial.dlegal.label: Legal approval
Denial.dlegal.city_config: Who may approve a denial (city routing); CT requires the custodian personally.

Denial.ncomm.label: Compose denial communication

denial.written_notice_required.summary: The RAO must provide written notice by first class or electronic mail of any denial of access, within 10 business days of receipt of the request.
denial.written_notice_required.clock_spec: within 10 business-days of receipt of the request

denial.reasons_and_citation_required.summary: A denial/withholding must identify the records withheld and provide the specific reasons, including the specific statutory exemption(s) or common-law privilege and its applicability to each withheld portion.

Where a record is withheld on a claim of attorney-client privilege, the written denial must provide a detailed description of the record, including the names of the author and recipients and, in general terms, the subject matter of the withheld information.

appeal.retained_optional.summary: The response/denial must include a statement informing the requester of the right of administrative appeal to the Supervisor under § 10A(a) and the right to seek judicial review by civil action in the superior court.

Denial.ncomm.city_config: Denial letter template — must satisfy every content element listed for the state.

production.format_and_medium.summary: The RAO must provide public records by electronic means unless the record is not available in electronic form or the requestor cannot receive/access a usable electronic form.
The RAO must, to the extent feasible, provide the record in the requestor's preferred format or, absent a preference, in a searchable, machine-readable format.
The RAO must provide electronic records in native form when possible, presuming machine-readable electronic copies unless the requester specifies otherwise.

production.no_duty_to_create_or_convert.summary: The RAO is not required to create a new public record to comply with a request; furnishing a segregable portion of an existing record is not creation of a new record.

eligibility.any_person.summary: A records access officer must permit inspection or furnish a copy of any public record to any requestor, without limiting access to a class of persons.

eligibility.no_purpose_requirement.summary: A records access officer may not require the requester to state the purpose of a request, except to determine a commercial purpose or to rule on a fee-waiver request.

eligibility.no_residency_requirement.summary: Access to public records is not conditioned on the requestor's residency or citizenship; any person may request regardless of state of residence.

Master.s2.label: Commercial-rate requested

classification.commercial_purpose.summary: 'Commercial purpose' means the sale/resale of a record or use of its information to advance the requester's strategic business interests for profit, excluding news, citizen oversight, and academic/scientific/journalistic/public research.

Master.s2.city_config: commercial_rate approval module (v1): same two modes as fee_waiver (intake_review | routed_task). Must decide at INTAKE — commercial classification changes the response clock in NJ (14-bd) and IL (recurrent/commercial track). Classification overriding a self-declaration is always communicated.

custody.referral_to_proper_custodian.summary: If sought records are not within its possession, custody, or control, the written response must identify those records and identify the agency or municipality that may possess them, if known.

acknowledgment.note: No statutory timer — city operational target only (soft-standard pattern S-002).

response.initial_decision_window.summary: If the entity will not fully produce within the initial timeframe (or will withhold), it must inform the requestor in writing not later than 10 business days after initial receipt.
response.initial_decision_window.clock_spec: 10 business-days from initial receipt of request

response.clock_computation.summary: For a written request, time computation begins on the first business day following the date of receipt; an oral request is deemed received the day it was made.
response.clock_computation.clock_spec: start event: first business day following receipt (written) / day made (oral)

response.clock_computation.summary: Calculation of time commences only for requests made in accordance with the request requirements (e.g., reasonable description, proper delivery).

response.extension_grounds.summary: The requestor may voluntarily agree to a response date beyond the statutory extended timeframes.

response.extension_length.summary: For a municipality, the reasonable production timeframe stated in the written response shall not exceed 25 business days following initial receipt of the request.
For a (state) agency, the reasonable production timeframe stated in the written response shall not exceed 15 business days following initial receipt of the request.

A records access officer may petition the Supervisor of Records for an extension of time as soon as practical and within 20 business days after initial receipt (or within 10 business days after a Supervisor determination that the record is public).
response.extension_length.clock_spec: within 20 business-days from initial receipt (or 10 business-days from Supervisor determination)

response.extension_length.summary: The Supervisor must issue a written decision on an RAO extension petition within 5 business days following receipt of the petition.
response.extension_length.clock_spec: 5 business-days from Supervisor's receipt of the petition

response.extension_limit.summary: Upon a showing of good cause, the Supervisor may grant a single extension to a municipality not to exceed 30 business days.
response.extension_limit.clock_spec: ceiling: single extension up to 30 business-days (municipality)

response.extension_limit.summary: Upon a showing of good cause, the Supervisor may grant a single extension to a (state) agency not to exceed 20 business days.
response.extension_limit.clock_spec: ceiling: single extension up to 20 business-days (agency)

response.extension_limit.summary: If the Supervisor finds a request is part of a series of contemporaneous requests that are frivolous or designed to intimidate/harass and not for broad public dissemination, the Supervisor may grant a longer extension or relieve the entity of its obligation to provide copies.
response.extension_limit.clock_spec: terminal: obligation to provide copies may be relieved (or a longer extension granted)

response.extension_notice.summary: Upon submitting the extension petition to the Supervisor, the RAO must furnish a copy of the petition to the requestor.

production.completion_window.summary: The RAO must permit inspection or furnish a copy (or any segregable portion) not later than 10 business days following receipt of the request.
Independent of the 10-day cap, production or inspection must occur at reasonable times and without unreasonable delay.
production.completion_window.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "at reasonable times and without unreasonable delay" from request receipt

clarification_response.note: No statutory timer — city operational target only (soft-standard pattern S-002).

payment.nonpayment_consequence.summary: A records access officer shall not charge a fee for a public record unless the RAO responded to the requestor within 10 business days under subsection (b).
payment.nonpayment_consequence.clock_spec: terminal: fee right is forfeited if no § 10(b) response within 10 business-days

payment.nonpayment_consequence.summary: The RAO may deny public-records requests from a requester who has failed to compensate the entity for previously produced public records.
When denying for an unpaid balance, the RAO shall provide written notification detailing the reasons, including an itemized list of balances attributed to previously produced records.

suspension.note: No statutory timer — city operational target only (soft-standard pattern S-002).

ag_referral.note: No statutory timer — city operational target only (soft-standard pattern S-002).

denial_deadline.note: No statutory timer — city operational target only (soft-standard pattern S-002).

fee.copy_rate_per_page.summary: The fee for standard black-and-white paper copies or printouts shall not exceed 5 cents per page, for both single- and double-sided copies.

fee.labor_charge.summary: For a municipality, the hourly labor rate must equal or be less than the lowest-paid capable employee's rate and shall not exceed $25 per hour, unless a higher rate is approved by the Supervisor.
For a (state) agency, the hourly labor rate must equal or be less than the lowest-paid capable employee's rate and shall not be more than $25 per hour.

The Supervisor may approve a petition to charge for segregation/redaction time, or a municipal petition to charge over $25/hour, if the request is for a commercial purpose or the fee is a necessary, reasonable good-faith cost not designed to deter access; the entity must furnish the petition to t…
fee.labor_charge.clock_spec: Supervisor written determination within 5 business-days of receipt of the petition

fee.actual_cost_basis.summary: A records access officer may assess a reasonable fee for production (except freely-inspectable records), and the fee shall not exceed the actual cost of reproducing the record.

fee.electronic_media_charge.summary: The actual cost of any storage device or material provided in response to a request may be included as part of the fee.

fee.free_allowance.summary: For a municipality with a population over 20,000, no labor fee may be assessed for the first 2 hours of work performed.
For a (state) agency, no labor fee may be assessed for the first 4 hours of work performed.

fee.no_charge_categories.summary: A fee shall not be assessed for time spent segregating or redacting records unless such segregation/redaction is required by law or approved by the Supervisor.

custody.records_officer_designation.summary: Each agency and municipality must designate one or more employees as records access officers to coordinate and respond to public-records requests.
In a municipality, the municipal clerk (or the clerk's designees, or any designee the chief executive officer appoints) serves as records access officer.

payment.advance_payment.summary: A records access officer may delay provision of records until all fees related to the request are paid in full by the person seeking access.
